findings.title: MetricsMiddleware shares a single mutable instance across all clients, causing a data race on the `next` field
findings.body: NewMetricsMiddleware creates one MetricsMiddleware instance (imw) and then, inside the ClientMiddlewareFunc closure, assigns `imw.next = next` every time the middleware is applied. In Grafana, the middleware chain is applied per plugin client (potentially many times, concurrently during plugin initialization and request handling). Multiple goroutines can therefore write to the same `imw.next` field simultaneously, and a request being served by one client can observe another client's `next` (or a partially written pointer), causing requests to be routed to the wrong plugin client or a fatal concurrent map/pointer race. The previous InstrumentationMiddleware had the same pattern, but the rename is a good opportunity to fix it. The middleware should return a new MetricsMiddleware per invocation (e.g., `return &MetricsMiddleware{pluginMetrics: imw.pluginMetrics, pluginRegistry: pluginRegistry, next: next}`) so each decorated client has its own immutable `next`.

findings.title: FromContext silently discards the context's logger when the type assertion fails
findings.body: grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext calls `d.l.FromContext(ctx)` and type-asserts the result to `*log.ConcreteLogger`. If the assertion fails (e.g., the context carries a different logger implementation, or infra log's FromContext returns a different type in some code path), the method falls back to `d.New()`, which returns a logger with only the wrapper's existing context — completely discarding whatever logger/attributes were stored in the provided ctx. At minimum this fallback should be more defensive (e.g., preserve the infra logger from context without the ConcreteLogger assertion, or log a warning).

The fake should either record the received context (e.g., store it in a field) or return a logger that captures FromContext calls, so tests can assert on context propagation. As written, it makes the new FromContext-based logging path effectively untestable with this fake.
